newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Villa sees strong demand for flotation.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Villa sees strong demand for flotation.

text.p: English premier league soccer club Aston Villa expects the institutional part of its flotation to be some three times oversubscribed, finance director Mark Ansell said on Thursday.

Ansell told Reuters that there was some nervousness among institutions about the soccer sector following recent share price falls. But he said he believed the club had got its message across and that demand would be strong.
"Institutions have distinguished Aston Villa from a number of other clubs in the sector," he said. "It is seen as a quality investment which is being run as a very good business."
Villa said earlier that it was seeking to raise 15.225 million stg, net of expenses, in a flotation valuing the company at 125.9 million stg.
The placing and offer price has been set at 11 stg and dealings are scheduled to begin on May 7.
The flotation will make Villa the fourth largest of 16 listed UK soccer clubs, behind Manchester United, Chelsea Village Plc and Newcastle United.
Newcastle joined the stock market earlier this month but their shares are now trading 10p below their 135p issue price.

Ansell said that Villa would have some 10 million stg available from the flotation to strengthen its squad this summer. The rest of the money is being spent on a 650-seat conference centre and two video screens to be installed at Villa Park in Birmingham.
Villa will decide next year whether to press ahead with plans to boost capacity from 40,000 to 50,000 but Ansell said it was likely that the club would do so.
The club is increasing season ticket prices by 14 percent next season. Ansell said the club had not put up prices last year and had some of the lowest prices among premier league clubs.
